title: Establishing and Classifying Benefit Overpayment Accounts
content:
Each of the Benefit Overpayment Accounts a claimant owes comes into existence through a written overpayment determination, and its classification follows from the finding on fault in that determination.

## The determination and the principal

An overpayment is established by a written determination naming the claim, the overpaid weeks, the cause and the classification. The principal is the total of benefits paid for those weeks that were not payable, gross of any offset or withholding taken from them. Benefits paid on a claim later confirmed as filed by an impostor are never established against the identity theft victim.

## Classification follows the finding on fault

| Finding | Classification |
|---|---|
| Agency processing or adjudication error; no fault on the claimant's part; information reported complete and accurate | Non-Fraud Overpayment — Agency Error |
| Employer wage or separation report error; no fault on the claimant's part; information reported complete and accurate | Non-Fraud Overpayment — Employer Reporting Error |
| Benefits paid when due and then reversed on appeal by a higher-level decision; no fault on the claimant's part | Non-Fraud Overpayment — Appeal Reversal |
| The claimant reported inaccurately without intent; no knowing misrepresentation found | Non-Fraud Overpayment — Claimant Error |
| Knowing false statement or concealment, with no prior fraud determination in the look-back | Fraud Overpayment — First Offense |
| Knowing false statement or concealment, with at least one prior fraud determination in the look-back | Fraud Overpayment — Repeat Offense |

Agency error, employer reporting error and reversal on appeal of benefits paid when due are without fault on the claimant's part; an inaccurate report without intent is claimant error; a knowing false statement or concealment is fraud. Fraud is a repeat offense when the count of prior fraud determinations is at least one. That count is the number of the claimant's other overpayments classified as a fraud overpayment, not cancelled, whose determination date falls within the repeat-offense look-back years before the new determination date.

## Mailing

The determination is mailed on its determination date with the appeal rights of the overpayment and fraud appeal docket and, where the classification allows waiver, the waiver request form.

## When recovery begins

Recovery begins only after the appeal deadline of the determination has passed with no appeal on record and, for waiver-eligible classifications, after the waiver window has passed with no waiver request under review. At that point the overpayment moves from established to in recovery. An overpayment whose balance reaches zero before recovery formally began is paid in full.

| Waiver-eligible classification | Appeal on record | Waiver request under review | Recovery begins after the deadlines pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | No | Yes, once both the appeal deadline and the waiver window have passed |
| No | No | — | Yes, once the appeal deadline has passed |
